content:
sam: Heads up — I'm seeing steady memory growth (~200MB/hour) when running the streaming chat path with a tool loop (external tool calls that append to context). Repro is pretty consistent on the nightly dedicated runner.

sam: Repro steps: start convo with long tool loop (~30 calls), streaming enabled, model=vicuna-13b-8k, dedup KV disabled. After ~10k tokens heap grows and doesn't fall. pmap shows resident climbs.

sam: Quick logs: 
```
[2026-02-10T09:12:34Z] stream: token 10240, kv_cache_size=1.9GB, rss=5.3GB
[2026-02-10T09:22:34Z] stream: token 20480, kv_cache_size=2.1GB, rss=5.5GB
```

sam: Attached pprof heap diff (heap_before->heap_after): big chunk of buffers under module `kv_store` and lots of 'mallocx' small allocations. Not obvious leak in our code; maybe fragmentation or reuse issue.

maria: Can you paste the pprof top and `jeprof --alloc_space` output? Also which allocator on that runner (jemalloc/tcmalloc)? If jemalloc we can dump `jemalloc.stats` and `mallctl` counters.

sam: It's jemalloc. Quick top of pprof: 
```
512MB  24.5%  24.5%  kv_store::KVBuffer::append
320MB  15.3%  39.8%  std::vector<...>::resize
240MB  11.5%  51.3%  protobuf::MessageLite::SerializeToString
```

ajay: Two hypotheses: 1) we keep allocating many small KV buffers per token and never reuse the slab, so fragmentation + jemalloc bin growth. 2) the paging/eviction path doesn't actually free underlying buffers when we evict (we drop refs but don't free the backing allocation).

ajay: Try forcing a full GC/arena free after a loop and see if RSS drops (quick check). If RSS doesn't drop but `kv_cache_size` reduces, it's fragmentation.

lucy: FWIW I saw similar behavior when streaming + tool loops with per-tool metadata. Disabling streaming (collect then emit) removed the growth. So likely streaming path keeps references to slices for longer.

perf-bot: [alert] perf/regression detected: build 2026-02-09 -> 2026-02-10, 12% rss increase on long-context tests (test: streaming-chat-tool-loop). Commit: 9f3c2a7 (kv: add stronger refcounts).

sam: Ooh that commit is the one that changed refcounting to avoid races. Maybe we introduced a path that increments refcount but doesn't decrement on early exits. Will bisect.

devon: I can pair on bisecting today. Meanwhile can you run `jeprof --inuse_space --base=before.heap after.heap` and upload flamegraphs? Also try `MALLOC_CONF=prof:true,lg_prof_sample:19` on a short repro to get clearer allocation sites.

sam: Uploaded heap dumps and flamegraph gist: https://internal/gists/kv-toolloop-flame

sam: Repro script (short): 
```
for i in {1..30}; do 
  ./runner --streaming --tool-loop 50 --model vicuna-13b
done
```

maria: Quick mitigation while we root cause: add a periodic prune() that runs every N tokens and calls `kv_store.compact()` which tries to merge small fragments and release backing buffers to the OS. Not ideal but buy time for a proper fix.

ajay: Another immediate workaround: change allocation for per-token KV to use a pooled arena per-request and release whole arena on end-of-request. That avoids jemalloc fragmentation. Patch sketch: 
```
// pseudocode
Arena& a = get_request_arena();
KVBuffer b = a.alloc_buffer();
b.append(...)
// on request end: a.reset(); // frees all in one go
```

lucy: Sounds good. Also check the eviction path: if we use `shared_ptr` for slices, make sure no background thread holds a copy (e.g., streaming writer lambda capturing by value). I've hit cases where callbacks retained buffers longer than expected.

sam: Found a suspicious pattern in streaming writer: `on_token([slice]{ queue.push(slice); })` — the lambda copies slice. If queue isn't drained promptly this could keep allocations alive. I'm adding move semantics and weak refs.

sam: Quick test after changing lambda to `on_token([slice=std::move(slice)]{ queue.emplace_back(std::move(slice)); })` — initial run shows slower growth (~50MB/hour). Not fixed but improved.

maria: Good find. Let's still run the bisect to see if commit 9f3c2a7 introduced a missing decrement on early-return paths. Also throw in `valgrind --leak-check=full` on a small run (if feasible) though slow.

devon: I'll start the bisect. If we confirm refcounting bug, we should add a unit test that simulates tool-loop + streaming and checks RSS differential under a threshold.

ajay: If anyone needs a quick patch to limit impact: set default `streaming.max_queued_slices=128` and `kv.prune_interval_tokens=5000` in config. That should cap retained slices and reduce cumulative growth.

sam: I'll land the streaming lambda change + config caps as a canary on nightly, then follow up with a proper arena/pool refactor if bisect points to fragmentation. I'll post updates here. Thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — ping me when you have bisect result.

sam: Update: bisect points to 9f3c2a7 as a contributor but root cause is interplay with the streaming lambda copying slices. PR incoming with fixes and a test.

sam: PR: https://internal/pulls/3127 — includes lambda move, pooling experiment behind flag, and a test that runs the tool-loop repro with --short and asserts RSS delta < 150MB.

lucy: Nice. Marking as in-progress. :rocket:
